Solved successfully (after 3 incorrect submissions) on 2026-11-01. Save this pattern as a possible recurring family.

Input consists of multiple solid 3-valued patches with scattered 2 markers. Each 2 marker embedded in/at a patch defines a 3×3 square centered on that marker; recolor the other cells in that square to 1, leaving the center marker 2. Multiple squares overlap by union. Some squares extend into background 0; those cells are also recolored 1 when they lie in the patch-associated region (demonstrations establish this). Preserve all cells outside the localized square overlays and preserve all other 2s.

Caution: my failed attempts came from misidentifying which markers belong to which patches and from using imprecise global-neighbor/rectangular-bound rules. Final successful output was equivalent to applying 3×3 neighborhoods for markers associated with the colored patches, preserving 2 centers, with no indiscriminate treatment of remote markers. In demonstrations, a marker within an irregularly bounded patch can paint 1s into adjacent background cells; so don't simply clip overlays to original 3 cells. Derive patch limits and marker association from the demos.

Demo evidence: repeated 2-marker centers within 3-patches produce local 3×3 blocks of 1 around/under the 2; two adjacent centers produce unioned adjacent blocks. Demo 3's marker at row 3 col 4 (0-indexed) caused a 3×3 region of 1 including a formerly 0 cell at row 2 col 5. Output keeps center 2s unchanged and untouched 3 patches remain 3.
